f.title: MAH EudraVigilance monitoring and validated-signal notification apply from 22 February 2018
f.statement: The requirement for MAHs to monitor EudraVigilance data (IX.C.1.1 and IX.C.3) and to inform the Agency and national competent authorities of validated signals (IX.C.4) enters into force on 22 February 2018 and, for a transition period, applies only to active substances in products on the additional monitoring list in force as of 22 November 2017.
f.applicability: Transition period: active substances in products on the additional monitoring list as of 22 November 2017

rows.quote: Note: The requirement for marketing authorisation holders to monitor EudraVigilance data (Sections IX.C.1.1. and IX.C.3.) and inform the Agency and national competent authorities of validated signals (Section IX.C.4.) will enter into force on 22 February 2018 and will only apply, for a transition period, to active substances contained in medicinal products included in the ‘List of medicinal products under additional monitoring’ in force as of 22 November 2017.
rows.review_note: Review: Checked: transitional entry-into-force note; level Mandatory kept because it sets the start date of the IR Art 18(2)/21(2) MAH duties for the transition scope. Double-check: Transitional entry-into-force note, not itself a duty; Mandatory is a judgement call (it dates the IR Art 18(2)/21(2) MAH duties). The transition period (additional-monitoring substances only) has since ended, so the scope restriction is historical. Currency: EMA GVP page (checked 2026-11-10) lists Module IX Rev. 1 (EMA/827661/2011, effective 22/11/2017) as current; Addendum I (EMA/209012/2015) is a separate companion document, not a replacement. No duplicate committed curation.

f.title: Own signal management process allowed if it encompasses the Module IX principles
f.statement: Individual organisations may follow alternative signal management processes and terminology but should encompass the general principles outlined in GVP Module IX.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: Individual organisations may follow alternative signal management processes and terminology but should encompass the general principles outlined in this Module.
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Permission to use own process/terminology, conditioned on encompassing the Module principles. Double-check: Mixed may/should; 'individual organisations' actor generic; Recommended taken from the should.

f.title: Consider only adverse-reaction signals when monitoring EudraVigilance
f.statement: For the purpose of monitoring data in EudraVigilance, only signals related to an adverse reaction shall be considered.

rows.quote: For the purpose of monitoring data in the EudraVigilance database (also referred to as ‘EudraVigilance’), only signals related to an adverse reaction shall be considered [IR Art 19(1)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Mandatory (shall, IR Art 19(1)) correct; scoping rule with no named actor (MAH inferred).

f.title: Consider all relevant data sources in signal management
f.statement: Although the module focuses on signals from spontaneous reporting systems, all relevant sources should be considered during signal management.
f.clause: IX.B.1. Sources of data and information

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: This module focusses mainly on signals originating from the monitoring of data from spontaneous reporting systems, however all relevant sources should be considered during signal management.
rows.location: IX.B.1. Sources of data and information
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote extended with its lead-in so it proves the 'although the module focuses on spontaneous reports' clause. Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Use a signal detection methodology suited to the data and product, with clinical judgement
f.statement: Signal detection should follow a methodology taking into account the nature of data and the characteristics and type of medicinal product (e.g. vaccines and biologicals may require specific strategies); data from all appropriate sources should be considered and clinical judgement should always be applied.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: Signal detection should follow a methodology which takes into account the nature of data and the characteristics (e.g. time on market, patient exposure, target population) as well as the type of medicinal product concerned (e.g. vaccines and biological medicinal products may for example require specific methodological strategies (see GVP P.I. and GVP P.II.)). Data from all appropriate sources should be considered (see IX.B.1.). Clinical judgement should always be applied.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred. Three shoulds merged; examples summarised.

f.title: Consider aggregated data where individual case assessment is not feasible
f.statement: Where it is not relevant or feasible to assess each individual case (e.g. signals from published studies or healthcare record data), assessment of aggregated data should be considered.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: When it is not relevant or feasible to assess each individual case (e.g. signals detected from published studies, healthcare record data), assessment of aggregated data should be considered.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Document the signal detection process
f.statement: The signal detection process should be adequately documented by each organisation.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: The signal detection process should be adequately documented by each organisation (see IX.B.5.).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Actor 'each organisation' named generically; Recommended correct.

f.title: Consider previous awareness, strength of evidence and clinical relevance when validating signals
f.statement: When performing signal validation based on review of ICSR data, the following should be considered: previous awareness (product information, SmPCs of other products with the substance, prior regulatory assessments), strength of evidence (e.g. number of supportive cases after excluding duplicates, exposure, related terms, consistency, data quality, case definitions, dose-reaction, mechanism, disproportionality) and clinical relevance and context (e.g. seriousness, outcome, interactions, vulnerable populations, patterns of use).
f.clause: IX.B.3. Evaluation during signal validation and further assessment

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: The following elements should be considered when performing signal validation based on the review of ICSR data:
rows.location: IX.B.3. Evaluation during signal validation and further assessment
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote is only the lead-in sentence; the element list in the statement (previous awareness, strength of evidence, clinical relevance) is bullet content not in the quote (over 1000 characters with line-end hyphens). Table/bullet-derived.

f.title: Document the signal evaluation decision tree
f.statement: Any decision tree used within an organisation's signal management process should be documented as part of the description of the signal management process.
f.clause: IX.B.3. Evaluation during signal validation and further assessment

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: Any such decision tree should be documented as part of the description of the signal management process (see IX.B.5.).
rows.location: IX.B.3. Evaluation during signal validation and further assessment
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote starts 'Any such decision tree' and relies on the preceding sentence. Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Assess throughout whether signals suggest risks with important public health or benefit-risk impact
f.statement: Every organisation should consider throughout signal management whether signals suggest risks with an important impact on patients' or public health and/or on the risk-benefit balance of the medicinal product.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: Every organisation should consider throughout the signal management process whether signals suggest risks with an important impact on patients’ or public health and/or on the risk-benefit balance of the medicinal product (see IX.A.1.1.).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Actor 'every organisation' generic; Recommended correct.

f.title: Consider timely risk minimisation measures at any stage of signal management
f.statement: Appropriate measures should be considered at any stage if the information suggests a risk requiring timely prevention or minimisation; such measures may be required before a formal assessment of the signal is concluded.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: Appropriate measures should be considered at any stage if the information available suggests that there could be a risk that requires prevention or minimisation in a timely manner (see GVP Module XVI). Such measures may be required before a formal assessment of the signal is concluded.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred. 'may be required' clause merged.

f.title: Document the signal management system and apply a quality management system
f.statement: Any signal management system should be clearly documented (roles, responsibilities, tasks, qualified staff, control and improvement), a quality management system should be applied to all signal management processes, and detailed procedures should be developed, documented and implemented, including the rationale for the method and periodicity of signal detection.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: Any signal management system should be clearly documented to ensure that the system functions properly and effectively, that the roles, responsibilities and required tasks are clear and standardised, that these tasks are conducted by staff with appropriate qualifications and expertise and that there are provisions for appropriate control and, when needed, improvement of the system. A system of quality management (see GVP Module I) should be applied to all signal management processes. Detailed procedures for this quality system should be developed, documented and implemented. This includes the rationale for the method and periodicity of signal detection activities.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred. Several shoulds merged into one row.

f.title: Keep an audit trail of signal management activities through a tracking system
f.statement: Through a tracking system, all organisations should keep an audit trail of signal management activities allowing traceability (dates, timeliness) and process control of all steps, including analyses, decisions and rationale.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: Through a tracking system, all organisations should keep an audit trail of signal management activities, allowing traceability (i.e. recording of dates and confirmation of timeliness) and process control of the details of all steps of signal management, including analyses, decisions and rationale.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Actor 'all organisations' generic; statement faithful.

f.title: Assign roles for documentation, QC and CAPA; train staff in signal management
f.statement: Organisational roles and responsibilities for signal management activities, including documentation, quality control and review, and CAPA, should be assigned and recorded, and staff should be specifically trained in signal management activities according to their roles.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: The organisational roles and responsibilities for the activities including maintenance of documentation, quality control and review, and for ensuring corrective and preventive action should be assigned and recorded. Each organisation should ensure that staff members are specifically trained in signal management activities in accordance with their roles and responsibilities (see GVP Module I).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Two shoulds merged; organisation actor generic.

f.title: Describe signal management in the PSMF and present performance indicators in its annex
f.statement: MAHs should include the description of the signal management process in the PSMF; system performance should be controlled and, when used, performance indicators should be presented in the PSMF annex.

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders should include the description of the signal management process in the pharmacovigilance system master file (see GVP Module II). The performance of the system should be controlled and, when used, performance indicators should be presented in the annex to the pharmacovigilance system master file [IR Art 3, 9(1)]
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: MAH and should named in the quote; second sentence passive (performance control).

f.title: Maintain a record management system ensuring traceability of safety concern investigations
f.statement: MAHs shall put in place a record management system for all pharmacovigilance documents ensuring their retrievability and the traceability of measures taken to investigate safety concerns, of investigation timelines and of decisions on safety concerns, including date and decision-making process.

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders shall put in place a record management system for all documents used for pharmacovigilance activities that ensures the retrievability of those documents as well as the traceability of the measures taken to investigate safety concerns, of the timelines for those investigations and of decisions on safety concerns, including their date and the decision-making process [IR Art 12(1)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH, shall (IR Art 12(1)) and the full duty; statement faithful.

f.title: Audit signal management regularly, including contractors; guarantee data confidentiality and integrity
f.statement: Signal management activities should be audited at regular intervals, including tasks performed by service providers and contractors; data and document confidentiality, security and validity (including integrity when transferred between organisations) should be guaranteed, and documentation demonstrating compliance should be available at any time.
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (and other organisations performing signal management)
rows.quote: As for any critical process, signal management activities should be audited at regular intervals, including tasks performed by any service providers and contractors (see GVP Module IV). Data and document confidentiality (per the applicable laws and regulations), security and validity (including data integrity when transferred between organisations) should be guaranteed. Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – Module IX (Rev 1) EMA/827661/2011 Rev 1 Page 10/25   Documentation demonstrating compliance with these requirements should be available at any time, including justification / evidence for the steps taken and decisions made.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote contains page-header text. Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Continuously monitor product safety and inform authorities of new information
f.statement: The MAH in the EU should continuously monitor the safety of its products and inform the authorities of any new information that might have an impact on the marketing authorisation, including information meeting the definition of an emerging safety issue.
f.clause: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU

rows.quote: The marketing authorisation holder in the EU should continuously monitor the safety of their medicinal products and inform the authorities of any new information that might have an impact on the marketing authorisation [DIR Art 23(2), REG Art 16(2)]. This includes information that meets the definition of an emerging safety issue (see IX.A.1.1. and IX.C.2.)
rows.location: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Level Mandatory is a judgement call: GVP wording is 'should' but the duty is cited to DIR Art 23(2)/REG Art 16(2).

f.title: Continuously monitor EudraVigilance and handle resulting signals per IX.C.3 and IX.C.4
f.statement: Continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance is a legal requirement in the EU; signals detected through it should be handled according to IX.C.3 and IX.C.4.
f.clause: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU

rows.quote: The continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance is a legal requirement in the EU [IR Art 18]. Signals detected through the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data should be handled according to the principles outlined in IX.C.3. and IX.C.4..
rows.location: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'is a legal requirement' (IR Art 18) plus a 'should' handling clause merged; actor inferred.

f.title: Handle signals from other sources via own process and report them appropriately
f.statement: Signals from sources other than EudraVigilance should be handled according to the MAH's own signal management process and reported to EU competent authorities as appropriate, taking into account the obligations to keep product information up to date by variations and to present comprehensive signal information in PSURs; the IX.C.4 options and timelines apply only to EudraVigilance signals.
f.clause: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU

rows.quote: Signals detected through other sources should be handled according to the marketing authorisation holder’s own signal management process, taking into account the general principles outlined in IX.B.. Such signals should be reported to the competent authorities in the EU as appropriate, taking into account the general obligations of the marketing authorisation holder to keep their product information up-to-date throughout the product’s lifecycle by variation applications and to present comprehensive signal information in PSURs (see GVP Module VII). The options and timelines outlined in IX.C.4. solely apply to signals detected through the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data.
rows.location: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Statement faithful; MAH named; Recommended correct.

f.title: Notify emerging safety issues from any source per IX.C.2
f.statement: Signals from any source that meet the definition of emerging safety issues should be notified to the Agency and the competent authorities in Member States in accordance with IX.C.2.
f.clause: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU

rows.quote: Signals, from any source, that meet the definition of emerging safety issues (see IX.A.1.1.) should be notified to the Agency and the competent authorities in Member States in accordance with the process outlined in IX.C.2..
rows.location: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Collaborate with PRAC by providing requested additional information
f.statement: The MAH should collaborate with the PRAC for the assessment of signals by providing the additional information requested.
f.clause: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU

rows.quote: The marketing authorisation holder should collaborate with the PRAC for the assessment of the signals by providing the additional information requested [DIR Art 23(4) and REG Art 16(3a)] (see IX.C.6.).
rows.location: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU

f.title: Keep product information up to date with scientific knowledge and published assessments
f.statement: MAHs shall keep their product information up to date in the light of scientific knowledge, including assessments and recommendations made public via the European medicines web-portal.
f.clause: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU
f.legal_basis: IR Art 11(1)(f); DIR Art 23(3); REG Art 16(3)
f.processes: Safety labeling; Submission operations; Signal management

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders shall keep their product information up-to-date in the light of scientific knowledge, including the assessments and recommendations made public via the European medicines web-portal [IR Art 11(1)(f), DIR Art 23(3), REG Art 16(3)] (see IX.C.9.).
rows.location: IX.C.1.1. Responsibilities of the marketing authorisation holder in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH, shall and the full duty (IR Art 11(1)(f), DIR Art 23(3), REG Art 16(3)).

f.title: Notify emerging safety issues in writing to NCAs and the Agency
f.statement: When the MAH in the EU becomes aware of an emerging safety issue from any source, it should notify it in writing to the competent authority(ies) of the Member State(s) where the product is authorised and to the Agency.

rows.quote: When the marketing authorisation holder in the EU becomes aware of an emerging safety issue from any source (see IX.A.1.1.), they should notify it in writing to the competent authority(ies) of Member State(s) where the medicinal product is authorised 11 and to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Statement trimmed: '(dedicated Agency mailbox)' is not in the quote. Quote contains footnote marker '11'.

f.title: Notify emerging safety issues no later than 3 working days after establishing they meet the definition
f.statement: When the MAH becomes aware of an emerging safety issue from any source, it should notify it in writing to the competent authority(ies) of the Member State(s) where the product is authorised and to the Agency, as soon as possible and no later than 3 working days after establishing that a validated signal or safety issue meets the definition of an emerging safety issue.

rows.deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 3 working days after establishing that the issue meets the definition
rows.quote: This should be done as soon as possible and no later than 3 working days after establishing that a validated signal or a safety issue from any source meets the definition of an emerging safety issue.

deadline_rule.clock_start: establishing that a validated signal or a safety issue from any source meets the definition of an emerging safety issue
deadline_rule.applies_to: Written notification of an emerging safety issue to the competent authorities and the Agency

f.title: Also submit ICSRs where the emerging safety issue is a single case
f.statement: Emerging safety issue notification is in addition to the ICSR submission requirements of GVP Module VI when the issue refers to a single case of suspected adverse reactions.

rows.quote: This is in addition to the ICSR submission requirements detailed in GVP Module VI, when the emerging safety issue refers to a single case of suspected adverse reactions.

f.title: Content of an emerging safety issue notification and follow-up information
f.statement: When notifying an emerging safety issue, the MAH should describe the safety issue, the source(s) of information and any planned or taken actions with timelines, provide relevant documentation available at initial notification, and provide further relevant information to the Agency and national competent authorities as soon as it becomes available.

rows.deadline: Further information as soon as it becomes available
rows.quote: When notifying an emerging safety issue, the marketing authorisation holder should describe the safety issue, the source(s) of information, any planned or taken actions with timelines, and should provide any relevant documentation available at the time of initial notification. data_elements: planned or taken actions with timelines

f.title: Provide a standalone signal notification for an emerging safety issue if requested
f.statement: For signals notified as emerging safety issues a standalone signal notification is not required, unless the authorities consider it appropriate to handle the issue within the EU signal management process, in which case the MAH may be requested to complete and provide a standalone signal notification form.

rows.quote: For signals notified as emerging safety issues, a standalone signal notification (see IX.C.4.3.) is not required, unless the national competent authorities and/or the Agency consider it appropriate to handle the issue within the EU signal management process, in which case the marketing authorisation holder may be requested to complete and provide a standalone signal notification form.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'is not required' / 'may be requested' - exemption with judgement on level.

f.title: Collaborate with authorities in assessing the emerging safety issue
f.statement: The MAH should collaborate with the Agency and national competent authorities in the assessment of the emerging safety issue.

rows.quote: The marketing authorisation holder should collaborate with the Agency and national competent authorities in the assessment of the emerging safety issue [DIR Art 23(4) and REG Art 16(3a)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Level Mandatory is a judgement call: wording is 'should', duty cited to DIR Art 23(4)/REG Art 16(3a).

f.title: Notify as emerging safety issues only concerns that cannot permit any delay
f.statement: MAHs should only communicate as emerging safety issues those safety concerns which meet the definition, i.e. whose urgency and seriousness cannot permit any delay in handling.

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders should only communicate as emerging safety issues those safety concerns which meet the definition provided in IX.A.1.1., i.e. whose urgency and seriousness cannot permit any delay in handling.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH and should; statement faithful.

f.title: Notify marketing cessation, withdrawal or non-renewal decisions in parallel
f.statement: Should the MAH decide, as a result of an emerging safety issue, on temporary or permanent cessation or suspension of marketing, withdrawal from the market, request for withdrawal of the marketing authorisation or non-application for renewal, the notification of such action should be done in parallel to the Agency.

rows.quote: Should the marketing authorisation holder decide as a result of the emerging safety issue to take any of the following actions: temporary or permanent cessation or suspension of marketing of a medicinal 11 See www.ema.europa.eu for e-mail addresses of Member States regarding emerging safety issues 12 See www.ema.europa.eu Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – Module IX (Rev 1) EMA/827661/2011 Rev 1 Page 12/25   product, withdrawal of a medicinal product from the market, request for the withdrawal of a marketing authorisation or non-application for the renewal of a marketing authorisation, the notification of such action should be done in parallel to the Agency

f.title: Do not notify quality defects or falsification issues as emerging safety issues
f.statement: New safety information related to quality defects or suspected falsified medicinal products which might influence the evaluation of benefits and risks and which may give rise to an abnormal restriction in supply should not be notified as an emerging safety issue.

rows.quote: New safety information related to quality defects or suspected falsified medicinal products which might influence the evaluation of the benefits and risks of the medicinal product and which may give rise to an abnormal restriction in supply should not be notified as an emerging safety issue.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Statement trimmed: 'but to the Agency and/or competent authorities according to national requirements' is not in the quote. Passive; MAH inferred.

f.title: Base identification of new or changed risks on signal detection and analysis
f.statement: The identification of new risks or changed risks shall be based on the detection and analysis of signals.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder, national competent authorities and the Agency
rows.quote: The identification of new risks or changed risks shall be based on the detection and analysis of signals [IR Art 19(1)].
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Legal basis for signal-based risk identification (IR Art 19(1)) was not captured. Double-check: Mandatory (shall, IR Art 19(1)) but no named actor; applies to all parties.

f.title: Monitor EudraVigilance data to the extent of access
f.statement: MAHs shall monitor the data available in the EudraVigilance database to the extent that they have access to the database.

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders shall monitor the data available in the EudraVigilance database to the extent that they have access to the database [IR Art 18 (2)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH, shall (IR Art 18(2)) and the full duty.

f.title: Request extended ICSR data access (level 2B) under a confidentiality undertaking
f.statement: MAHs can access all data elements of ICSRs they sent or resulting from the Agency's literature monitoring (ICSR Level 3); for other ICSRs they can request access to an extended subset including the narrative (ICSR data set level 2B) upon signing a confidentiality undertaking and confirming that review is required due to pharmacovigilance obligations.

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders can access without restrictions all data elements of those ICSRs sent by them or resulting from the medical literature monitoring activities performed by the Agency pursuant to Article 27 of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 (‘ICSR Level 3’). For other ICSRs held in EudraVigilance, marketing authorisation holders can request access to an extended subset of ICSR data elements including case narrative (‘ICSR data set level 2B’), upon signature of a confidentiality undertaking and confirmation that a review of ICSR data is required due to pharmacovigilance obligations, including in the context of signal management.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Access rights description ('can access') rather than a duty; Permitted is a judgement call; ICSR level terms quoted correctly.

f.title: Train staff on EudraVigilance outputs and document the training
f.statement: Relevant staff should familiarise themselves with the Agency's guidance and training materials on EudraVigilance outputs, and the training should be documented in line with internal procedures.

rows.quote: Relevant staff members within competent authorities and marketing authorisation holders should familiarise themselves with the guidance and training materials on EudraVigilance outputs made available online by the Agency and the training should be documented in line with the organisation’s internal procedures (see IX.B.5.).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: MAH and CA staff named; Recommended correct; 'the Agency's' added from 'made available online by the Agency'.

f.title: Monitor EudraVigilance continuously at a frequency proportionate to risk
f.statement: MAHs (as well as national competent authorities and the Agency) shall ensure continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance with a frequency proportionate to the identified and potential risks and the need for additional information.

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders, the national competent authorities and the Agency shall ensure the continuous monitoring of the EudraVigilance database with a frequency proportionate to the identified risk, the potential risks and the need for additional information on medicinal products or active substances [IR Art 18(3)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH, shall (IR Art 18(3)) and the proportionate-frequency duty; statement faithful.

f.title: Monitor EudraVigilance at least every 6 months; more often for additional monitoring products
f.statement: It is recommended to monitor EudraVigilance data at least every 6 months, and more frequently for active substances in products on the additional monitoring list, unless the sole reason for listing is a PASS request.
f.exceptions: More frequent monitoring not needed where the sole reason for additional monitoring is a PASS request.

rows.quote: It is recommended to monitor EudraVigilance data at least every 6 months. A more frequent monitoring is recommended for active substances contained in medicinal products included in the additional monitoring list in accordance with Article 23 of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 (see GVP Module X), unless the sole reason for inclusion on the list is the request of a post-authorisation safety study (PASS).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'It is recommended' with no named actor; 6-month frequency correct.

f.title: Determine and document the monitoring frequency per substance with justification
f.statement: Each organisation should determine the appropriate monitoring frequency for each active substance/product it monitors in EudraVigilance, and the frequency (including changes) and justification should be documented according to internal procedures.

rows.quote: Each organisation should determine the appropriate frequency for each active substance / medicinal product they monitor in EudraVigilance, taking into account the above-mentioned elements. The monitoring frequency (including any changes) and the justification thereof should be documented in accordance with the organisation’s internal procedures (see also IX.B.5.).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'Each organisation' actor generic; statement faithful.

f.title: Select drug-event combinations for review by scientific judgement, not SDRs alone
f.statement: The selection of drug-event combinations from EudraVigilance for further review should be based on scientific judgement, taking into account e.g. the number of cases and relevant statistical measures, the known safety profile, the clinical relevance (e.g. important medical events), the underlying condition, the patient population and previous assessments. Not all signals of disproportionate reporting have to be further investigated, and some drug-event combinations that are not signals of disproportionate reporting may warrant further investigation.

rows.quote: The selection of drug-event combinations for further review should be based on scientific judgement taking into account, e.g. the number of cases and relevant statistical measures, the known safety profile of the medicinal product, the clinical relevance (e.g. important medical events), the underlying condition, the patient population and previous assessments. Not all signals of disproportionate reporting have to be further investigated and conversely, some drug-event combinations that do not appear as signals of disproportionate reporting may warrant further investigation.
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Criteria for selecting drug-event combinations from EudraVigilance outputs were not captured. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred. Scientific-judgement criteria; partly descriptive.

f.title: Judge which products a signal applies to; consider all relevant ICSRs
f.statement: Scientific judgement should determine whether a signal applies to all or only some products with the substance, and MAHs should consider all ICSR data relevant to their product.

rows.quote: Scientific judgement should be applied to determine whether a particular signal may apply to all, or only some medicinal products containing an active substance. Marketing authorisation holders should consider in their analysis all ICSR data that are relevant to the safety profile of their medicinal product.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: First sentence passive; second names MAH.

f.title: Perform thorough EudraVigilance analysis for validation and manage records per procedures
f.statement: For signal validation, a thorough analysis of EudraVigilance data should be performed, considering previous awareness, strength of evidence (including narratives) and clinical relevance; record management for monitoring and analysis should follow internal procedures.

rows.quote: For the purpose of signal validation, a thorough analysis of EudraVigilance data should be performed taking into account any previous awareness on the signal, the strength of evidence from the cases (including narrative information) and the clinical relevance (see IX.B.3. and IX.C.4.). 14 see www.ema.europa.eu Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – Module IX (Rev 1) EMA/827661/2011 Rev 1 Page 14/25   Record management in relation to the monitoring and analysis of EudraVigilance data should be performed in line with the organisation’s internal procedures (see IX.B.5.).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote contains footnote and page-header text. Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Validate EudraVigilance signals and inform the Agency and NCAs forthwith
f.statement: Where a MAH detects a new signal when monitoring EudraVigilance, it shall validate it and shall forthwith inform the Agency and national competent authorities.
f.clause: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data

rows.quote: Where a marketing authorisation holder detects a new signal when monitoring the Eudravigilance database, it shall validate it and shall forthwith inform the Agency and national competent authorities [IR Art 21(2)].
rows.location: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH, shall (IR Art 21(2)), validation and forthwith notification.

f.title: Complement EudraVigilance analysis with own data; check other EU product information
f.statement: MAH signal validation should include a thorough EudraVigilance analysis, complemented for validated signals by assessment of other data available to the MAH; the MAH should check whether the risk is already addressed in the product information of other EU products with the substance (in which case product information should be aligned by variation).
f.clause: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data

rows.quote: For this purpose, signal validation by the marketing authorisation holder should include a thorough analysis of EudraVigilance data (see IX.B.3. and IX.C.3.3.). This analysis should be complemented, for validated signals, by the marketing authorisation holder’s assessment of other relevant data available to them (e.g. own database, literature, clinical trials) (see IX.B.3.). By definition, a signal should provide new information on an association (see IX.A.1.1.) and therefore, the marketing authorisation holder should check, wherever possible, whether a risk may already be addressed in the product information of other EU medicinal products containing the active substance of interest (except for product-specific issues), in which case the product information should be aligned as appropriate through an application for variation of the terms of marketing authorisation.
rows.location: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: MAH named; three shoulds merged; variation clause passive.

f.title: Take into account signal information published or communicated by the Agency
f.statement: When assessing signals detected in EudraVigilance, the marketing authorisation holder should also take into account the information published or communicated by the Agency in relation to signals (see IX.C.9).
f.clause: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data

rows.quote: The marketing authorisation holder should also take into account the information published or communicated by the Agency in relation to signals (see IX.C.9. and Figures IX.3. and IX.4. in IX. Appendix 1.).
rows.location: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Duty to consider Agency-published signal information was not captured. Double-check: MAH and should named; the EudraVigilance context comes from the surrounding section.

f.title: Day 0 for signal timelines; new or changed risks in principle by variation
f.statement: The conclusion that a signal represents a new or changed risk and/or that further analysis by the competent authorities is required is Day 0 of the timelines. A new or changed risk requiring a change to the terms of the marketing authorisation should in principle be the object of a variation application, unless the MAH considers that further analysis by the competent authorities is warranted.
f.clause: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data

rows.deadline: Day 0 = conclusion that the signal is a new or changed risk and/or needs further authority analysis
rows.quote: The conclusion that a signal represents a new or changed risk and/or that further analysis by the competent authorities is required is the starting point (‘Day 0’) of the timelines indicated herein. A new or changed risk that requires a change to the terms of the marketing authorisation should in principle be the object of an application for variation of the terms of marketing authorisation (see IX.C.4.1.), unless the marketing authorisation holder considers that further analysis by the competent authorities is warranted.
rows.location: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Day 0 definition merged with a 'should in principle' variation route.

f.title: Report signals needing authority analysis in PSURs only if conditions met; otherwise standalone
f.statement: Signals requiring further analysis by the competent authorities may be reported only in PSURs if the IX.C.4.2 conditions are met; if not, a standalone signal notification should be submitted. Refuted signals should only be reported in PSURs.
f.clause: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data

rows.quote: Signals requiring further analysis by the competent authorities may be reported only in PSURs if the conditions outlined in IX.C.4.2. are met. If not, a standalone signal notification should be submitted (see IX.C.4.3.). Refuted signals should only be reported in PSURs (see GVP Module VII).
rows.location: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred. may/should merged.

f.title: Report validated signals requiring urgent attention as emerging safety issues
f.statement: All validated signals requiring urgent attention should be reported as emerging safety issues.
f.clause: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data

rows.quote: All validated signals requiring urgent attention should be reported as emerging safety issues
rows.location: IX.C.4. Notifications and procedural options for signals detected by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU based on the continuous monitoring of EudraVigilance data
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Submit signal variations within 3 months (important risks) or 6 months (others)
f.statement: Where the MAH concludes from a EudraVigilance signal that the product information and/or RMP should be updated, it should submit the variation as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after completing the signal assessment if it corresponds to an important risk, or within 6 months for adverse reactions or risks not considered important; no separate standalone notification is then required.
f.clause: IX.C.4.1. Variation of the terms of marketing authorisation
f.processes: Safety labeling; Submission operations; Signal management

rows.deadline: No later than 3 months after completing the signal assessment (important risk); within 6 months (other adverse reactions/risks)
rows.quote: A marketing authorisation holder may conclude, based on their assessment of a signal detected through the monitoring of EudraVigilance data, that the product information and/or the RMP should be updated through a variation. In such cases, the marketing authorisation holder should submit the variation application to the relevant competent authorities as soon as possible and no later than 3 Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – Module IX (Rev 1) EMA/827661/2011 Rev 1 Page 15/25   months after completing the assessment of the signal if it corresponds to an important risk (see GVP Annex I), or within 6 months for adverse reactions or risks not considered important. In such instances, a separate standalone signal notification (see IX.C.4.3.) is not required, as the proposed changes and supportive evidence will be assessed within the variation procedure by the relevant competent authorities, which may consult the PRAC if required.
rows.location: IX.C.4.1. Variation of the terms of marketing authorisation
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote contains page-header text; 3-month/6-month deadlines correct.

f.title: Follow variations guidance and liaise with authorities when preparing the variation
f.statement: MAHs should follow the relevant guidance on variations, including worksharing procedures, and liaise with competent authorities as appropriate when preparing their variation application.
f.clause: IX.C.4.1. Variation of the terms of marketing authorisation
f.processes: Safety labeling; Submission operations; Signal management

rows.quote: Marketing authorisation holders should follow the relevant guidance on variations, including worksharing procedures, and liaise with competent authorities as appropriate when preparing their variation application
rows.location: IX.C.4.1. Variation of the terms of marketing authorisation
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH and should; statement faithful.

f.title: No standalone notification where a PSUR is due within 6 months of signal assessment
f.statement: If the substance is on the EURD list and a PSUR is due within 6 months of completing the signal assessment, the submission of a separate standalone signal notification is not required.
f.clause: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)

rows.deadline: PSUR due within 6 months of completing the signal assessment
rows.quote: If an active substance is included in the List of Union Reference Dates and Frequency of Submission of Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs) (EURD List) 16 and a PSUR is due to be submitted within 6 months of the completion, by the marketing authorisation holder, of the assessment of a signal detected through continuous EudraVigilance monitoring, the submission of a separate standalone signal notification (see IX.C.4.3.) is not required.
rows.location: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Exemption with no modal ('is not required'); 6-month PSUR window correct.

f.title: Mention signals assessed after the PSUR data lock point in the late-breaking information section
f.statement: If the data lock point of the PSUR has elapsed by the time the marketing authorisation holder has completed its assessment of the signal, the signal should be mentioned in the PSUR section indicated by the source (see GVP Module VII).
f.clause: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)

rows.quote: If the data-lock point of the PSUR has elapsed by the time the marketing authorisation holder has completed their assessment of the signal, it should be mentioned in the PSUR section
rows.location: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Late-breaking handling of signals assessed after the PSUR data lock point was not captured. Quote stops before the line-end hyphenated "Late-breaking"; the section name is taken from the next words of the source. Double-check: Statement trimmed to the quote: 'on late-breaking information together with a proposal for further management' is not in the quote, which stops before the line-end hyphenated 'Late-breaking'.

f.title: Draw PSUR conclusions on changes to the marketing authorisation, including from signals
f.statement: Based on the evaluation of cumulative safety data and the risk-benefit analysis in the PSUR, the MAH shall draw conclusions on the need for changes to the terms of the marketing authorisation and/or actions, including implications for the product information; this also applies to conclusions based on signal evaluation.
f.clause: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)

rows.quote: Based on the evaluation of the cumulative safety data and the risk-benefit balance analysis submitted in the PSUR, the marketing authorisation holder shall draw conclusions regarding the need for changes to the terms of the marketing authorisation and/or actions, including any implications for the approved product information for the medicinal product(s) for which the PSUR has been submitted [IR Art 34(5)]. This also applies to the conclusions drawn based on the evaluation of safety signals (see GVP Module VII).
rows.location: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote names MAH, shall (IR Art 34(5)) and covers the signal clause.

f.title: Report all validated signals and emerging safety issues concluded or ongoing in the PSUR
f.statement: Regardless of source, all validated signals and emerging safety issues whose evaluation was concluded during the PSUR reporting interval, or ongoing at the data lock point, should be reported in that PSUR (sections 15 and 16).
f.clause: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)

rows.quote: Regardless of their source, all validated signals and emerging safety issues for which the evaluation was concluded during the reporting interval of a PSUR, or are ongoing at the time of a PSUR data lock point, should be reported in that PSUR (PSUR sections 15 and 16) (see GVP Module VII).
rows.location: IX.C.4.2. Inclusion of the signal in the periodic safety update report (PSUR)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Passive voice; actor inferred.

f.title: Use the standalone signal notification form and send it to the Agency
f.statement: When a marketing authorisation holder, based on its assessment of a signal detected through EudraVigilance monitoring that does not meet the conditions outlined in IX.C.4.1 and IX.C.4.2, concludes that further analysis of the signal by the competent authorities is required, it should complete the standalone signal notification form available on the European medicines web-portal and send it to the Agency using the mailbox.

rows.quote: When a marketing authorisation holder, based on their assessment of a signal detected through EudraVigilance monitoring, and which does not meet the conditions outlined in IX.C.4.1. and IX.C.4.2., concludes that further analysis of the signal by the competent authorities is required, they should complete the standalone signal notification form available on the European medicines web-portal 17 and send it to the Agency using the mailbox
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. The NCAs as recipients follow in the source after the address and are also covered by 0040. Double-check: Statement trimmed to the quote: the competent authorities as additional recipients follow after the e-mail address and are not in the quote; 'dedicated' removed.

f.title: Submit a standalone signal notification within 30 days
f.statement: When the MAH concludes that further authority analysis of a EudraVigilance signal is required and IX.C.4.1/IX.C.4.2 do not apply, it should complete the standalone signal notification form and send it to the Agency and the competent authorities of Member States where the product is authorised, as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after completing the assessment.
f.systems: Standalone signal notification form; European medicines web-portal

rows.deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after completing the assessment
rows.quote: This should be done as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after the marketing authorisation holder has completed their assessment and concluded that further analysis by the competent authorities is required.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote starts 'This should be done' - the recipients and form come from the preceding sentence (row 0059); 30-day deadline correct.

f.title: Do not send refuted signals as standalone notifications; include them in PSURs
f.statement: Signals refuted by MAHs should not be sent as standalone signal notifications but should be included in PSURs as applicable.

rows.quote: Signals refuted by marketing authorisation holders should not be sent as standalone signal notifications but should be included in PSURs as applicable (see GVP Module VII).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Recommended correct; MAH implied by 'signals refuted by marketing authorisation holders'.

f.title: Provide PRAC-requested signal data (cumulative review), standard timeframe two months
f.statement: MAHs shall collaborate with the PRAC by providing the additional information requested, usually a cumulative review of relevant data with the MAH's discussion and conclusion; the standard timeframe is two months for submission of additional data by MAHs.
f.clause: IX.C.6. Signal analysis, prioritisation and assessment by the PRAC

rows.deadline: Standard timeframe: two months for submission of additional data
rows.quote: The standard timeframe is two months for the submission of additional data by marketing authorisation holders and a further two months for assessment by the PRAC. Depending on the signal multiple rounds of assessment may be needed. Timetables for signal assessment are published on the Agency’s website. Marketing authorisation holders shall collaborate with the PRAC for the assessment of the signals by providing the additional information requested [DIR Art 23(4) and REG Art 16(3a)]. Such requests are generally addressed to marketing authorisation holders of the reference medicinal products and usually consist of a cumulative review of relevant data (e.g. from spontaneous reports, clinical trials, scientific literature), together with a discussion and conclusion from the marketing authorisation holder.
rows.location: IX.C.6. Signal analysis, prioritisation and assessment by the PRAC
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Shall (DIR Art 23(4), REG Art 16(3a)) with MAH named; two-month timeframe merged from a descriptive sentence.

f.title: Implement PRAC signal recommendations (data, PSUR review, variation, RMP, RMM, PASS)
f.statement: Following PRAC recommendations, the MAH should as applicable provide additional data within a signal procedure; review the signal in the next PSUR or submit an ad-hoc PSUR; update the product information by variation; submit or update the RMP; implement additional risk minimisation measures such as educational materials or a DHPC; or sponsor a post-authorisation study and submit its final results.
f.clause: IX.C.7. Recommendations on signals from the PRAC

rows.quote: the marketing authorisation holder should provide additional data for assessment within a signal procedure; • the marketing authorisation holder should provide a review of additional data on the signal in the following PSUR or submit an ad-hoc PSUR (see GVP Module VII); • the marketing authorisation holder should update the product information through an application for a variation to the terms of the marketing authorisation; • the marketing authorisation holder should be requested to submit an RMP or to update the RMP (see GVP Module V); • the marketing authorisation holder should implement additional risk minimisation measures such as educational materials (see GVP Module XVI) or the dissemination of a Direct Healthcare Professional Communication (DHPC) (see GVP Module XV); • the marketing authorisation holder should sponsor a post-authorisation study according to an agreed protocol and submit the final results of that study (see GVP Module VIII);
rows.location: IX.C.7. Recommendations on signals from the PRAC
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Bullet list without its lead-in; quote truncated at 1000 characters; RMP item reads 'should be requested' (authority action).

dates.title: GVP Module IX Rev 1: comes into effect

dates.quote: Date for coming into effect of Revision 1* 22 November 2017

dates.scope: Marketing authorisation holders: monitoring of EudraVigilance data (IX.C.1.1., IX.C.3.) and informing the Agency and national competent authorities of validated signals (IX.C.4.); during a transition period only for active substances in products on the additional monitoring list in force as of 22 November 2017
